description: Direct check on claim-snapshot-install-stale-watermark. A follower is built on the real in-memory stores with the log store marked monotonically indexed, seeded with log entries 1..10 (watermark (10,1), snapshot index 0), and then driven with a well-formed InstallSnapshotRequest whose LastLogIndex is 4, whose payload is a genuine msgpack FSM snapshot, and whose configuration carries the node as a voter. installSnapshot therefore restores the snapshot, sets lastApplied=4 and lastSnapshot=(4,1), and takes the removeOldLogs branch that clears the whole log store - with no setLastLog. The observation compares the follower's own log watermark with the installed snapshot index after the handler returned success.

harness.description: Package-internal Go test that seeds a real InmemStore wrapped to report IsMonotonic()=true, builds Raft with skipStartup, starts only the real runFSM consumer so the snapshot restore can complete, invokes installSnapshot directly on the main-thread path with a real msgpack FSM payload, and emits the installed snapshot index, the store's last index and the follower's own watermark as CA_EVENT records.
semantic_changes: The LogStore is the real InmemStore with only IsMonotonic() added, so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch that clears the log; no read, write, delete or compaction logic is replaced.

The Raft instance is created with the internal skipStartup flag, then only the genuine runFSM goroutine is started so the handler's restore request can be consumed; the main loop and the snapshotter do not run, and installSnapshot is invoked directly as the main-thread handler.
The snapshot payload is produced with the package's own msgpack encoder so the real MockFSM.Restore path succeeds; the RPC framing layer is bypassed.

legality.derivation: The handler under test is reached with a snapshot version and term the implementation accepts (SnapshotVersion=1, term = currentTerm+1), a payload whose length equals the declared Size, and a configuration that decodes through the package's own encoding. The only substitution is bypassing Transport/processRPC and starting runFSM directly, which preserves the handler, the snapshot store, the FSM restore and the log-store clear.
legality.applicability: Applies to a follower whose in-memory log watermark index exceeds the installed snapshot's LastLogIndex; the entry is not reached when the follower is strictly behind the snapshot.
unresolved: Whether such a follower/snapshot pairing is reachable from legal leader behavior is not exercised; the fixture establishes the handler's own behavior given that state.

grounding.derivation: The result event reports the follower's own log watermark from getLastLog/getLastIndex together with the installed snapshot index and the store's last index at the same observation point, so one correlated event carries both sides of the post-install consistency relation.
grounding.applicability: Only observations whose store_after_install prerequisite reports install_succeeded=true are applicable; the trigger selects those results.

observable_properties.description: After a successful InstallSnapshot that cleared the log store, the follower's own log watermark index must be the installed snapshot index, not the pre-install watermark; a greater value means the follower reports log entries the install removed.

uncertainties: The oracle equates the post-install watermark with the installed snapshot index; in this fixture the store was cleared, so the snapshot index is the only consistent value, but the check does not distinguish a reset watermark that is lower than the snapshot index.
The check observes one follower, one snapshot index and the monotonic-store branch; the non-monotonic compaction branch and the leader-side nextIndex recovery are not exercised.
